recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-32583 unless a later work-group decision separately changes the historical format-* search parameter surface.
issue_request: FHIR-32583 was a Published OO change request for R5 asking whether DocumentReference.content.format should become an extension. The final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution instead renamed .format to .profile, made the element repeatable, represented the choices through a repeating backbone with value[x], allowed Coding, uri, and canonical, and added guidance that FHIR content should use canonical URLs of the StructureDefinition profiles the content complies with.
initial_application: The apparent initial application is git commit 56832a9e59e07d5449776a61dbb3d0ec3cd0f3d2, which changed DocumentReference.content.format 0..1 Coding into DocumentReference.content.profile 0..* BackboneElement with value[x] 1..1 typed Coding, uri, and canonical and added the FHIR profile-canonical comment. The commit subject did not name FHIR-32583, but the patch directly implements its resolution.
additional_context: DocumentReference is active in source/fhir.ini. The current R4 conversion map records DocumentReference.content.format -> content.profile, examples use <profile>, and DocumentReference search parameter expressions target DocumentReference.content.profile.value[x]. Confluence search found OO records for FHIR-32583 being resolved in January 2022 and included in a March 2022 DocumentReference update/pull-request agenda. Zulip search found general format/profile terminology discussion but no conflicting final decision.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The authoritative current source already has DocumentReference.content.profile at 0..* with value[x] typed Coding, uri, and canonical and includes the FHIR profile canonical usage note. Remaining format strings are aliases, XDS/IHE formatCode mappings, format-* search parameter identifiers/descriptions with expressions against content.profile, the conversion map, or commented historical notes rather than stale active content.format elements.
